balance_note: Fe II minus Fe I on the SAME band, instrument, holding, tier, selector, route and treatment — one scale by construction, so no correction is applied to either side and no value is re-derived (RYA-161). 7 of 10 matched pairs sit inside the Fe II reported bar; the VIS 1D-NLTE (Bergemann) pairs agree to +0.0630, +0.0350, +0.0340 dex. Closest pair: solar_kpno_molecfit_corrected VIS ENGINE-A at +0.0340 dex (Fe II 7.460 n=3 vs Fe I 7.426 n=104). ⚠️ The Fe II bars are wide — dominated by line-to-line scatter over n=3 — so 'consistent' here means the balance does not CONTRADICT the Fe I anchor, not that it constrains it.
anchor_caveat: ⚠️ DO NOT quote the Fe II VIS cells against the 7.466 anchor directly. That anchor is on the 3D-NLTE (gold v3, RYA-553) scale and these are 1D-NLTE products; comparing them mixes two scales, which is the RYA-669 ratchet the RYA-783 report warns about in as many words. The coincidence is inviting -- the kurucz2005 Fe II cell is 7.466 to three decimals, the anchor's own digits -- and a number that looks right on arrival is the one that never gets challenged. The defensible statement is the scale-matched balance above.
verdict: CLEAN — every live Fe II product carries the limit, none takes departures from the Gerber deck, and no Fe II per-line row is on an NLTE scale
